notes.meaning: The Lord announces that He is stirring up a destroying spirit against Babylon and its people. The name Leb-kamai was an ancient code name meaning Chaldea, pointing to the very heart of the empire that opposed God. No human strength can stop the judgment the Lord prepares to unleash.

Foreign invaders are compared to winnowers on a threshing floor who toss harvested wheat into the breeze so the wind blows away the chaff. These enemies will attack Babylon from every side when its day of disaster arrives. They will strip the mighty empire clean and leave the land completely empty.

The attacking soldiers are commanded to strike swiftly and give Babylon's defenders no time to draw their bows or put on coats of mail. The Lord orders that no young fighters be spared and that the entire army be wiped out. Human armor cannot protect anyone when God calls for judgment.

Babylon's warriors will fall dead across the land of the Chaldeans and lie pierced through in their own city streets. The strong forces that once terrorized the world will be powerless to protect their home. God's word against the proud city will be carried out completely.

Israel and Judah seemed like widows left entirely alone during their bitter years of exile. Yet the Lord of Hosts has not abandoned or divorced His people. Even though their land had been filled with sin and suffered heavy punishment, their covenant God remains committed to saving them.

The Jewish captives are warned to run for their lives and leave Babylon without delay. If they linger behind in the city, they risk being swept away in the punishment coming on its wickedness. God's time of vengeance has arrived to pay Babylon back for what it has done.

Babylon was once like a splendid gold cup in the Lord's hand, used by Him to pour out His anger on neighboring nations. The surrounding kingdoms suffered so horribly under Babylon's crushing power that they were left staggering like drunkards. Even the most powerful empire is only an instrument under God's control.

Babylon will fall suddenly and shatter like a glass dropped on stone. The call to wail and bring healing medicine is spoken with bitter irony, showing that the city's wound is beyond all help. Its ruin is final, and no human effort can save it.

Babylon's foreign allies and helpers realize that no medicine or military force can rescue the dying empire. They urge one another to give up and return home to their own countries. God's judgment against Babylon is so great that it towers all the way to the skies.

The Lord's people rejoice because He has vindicated them and proven that their trust in Him was right. By bringing down their cruel captors, God shows the whole world that He cares for His chosen flock. The exiles encourage each other to travel home to Jerusalem and tell everyone in Zion what God has done.

The attackers are told to sharpen their arrows and fill their quivers for battle. The Lord has stirred up the kings of the Medes to march against Babylon and tear it down. This destruction is the Lord's vengeance for the burning and ruin of His temple in Jerusalem.

War banners are raised to direct the siege, double the guards, and lay ambushes around Babylon. Whether this is an ironical taunt to the city's defenders or orders to the attackers, the outcome is certain. The Lord has planned this downfall, and He will accomplish every word He spoke.

Babylon felt secure because it was surrounded by the Euphrates River, broad canals, and vast wealth taken from other nations. Yet all its water barriers and riches cannot protect it from the end God has decreed. The thread of Babylon's life has reached its final measure and will now be cut.

The Lord of Hosts makes the most serious pledge possible by swearing by His own life. He promises that invading troops will swarm into Babylon as thick as a plague of locusts. These foreign soldiers will overrun the city and raise their shouts of victory over its ruins.

The prophet turns to praise the true God to remind the exiles of His unmatched power. The Lord made the earth by His mighty strength, set the world in place by His wisdom, and spread out the heavens by His understanding. A God who created the universe is more than able to bring down any human empire.

When the Lord speaks, thunder rumbles and rain waters pour from the skies. He draws up misty clouds from the ends of the earth, pairs flashing lightning with the downpour, and releases the winds from His storehouses. Nature itself obeys His command, proving that He alone rules the world.

Anyone who bows down to a handmade idol is shown to be foolish and without true understanding. Craftsmen who shape metal statues will be utterly disgraced by their creations. These molten images are complete frauds that have no life or breath in them.

False gods are entirely worthless and deserve nothing but mockery. They can neither hear prayers nor save themselves from ruin. When the Lord's time of punishment arrives, every idol will be shattered and perish.

The God of Jacob is completely different from useless idols, because He is the Maker of everything in heaven and on earth. He chose Israel as the tribe of His special inheritance, and His name is the Lord of Hosts. His people can rest securely knowing their God rules over all creation.

The Lord speaks of a chosen instrument as His war club or battle axe used to smash nations and overthrow kingdoms. God raises up earthly powers to execute His justice and bring proud rulers to ruin. Even the fiercest warriors are only tools held in His sovereign hand.

With this battle club, the Lord shatters the strongest parts of an ancient military force. War horses and their skilled riders are knocked down, while combat chariots and their drivers are destroyed. No weapon or cavalry can stand firm when God determines to tear them down.
